profile.name: GDP
profile.what: Quarterly economic growth, annualised. Released 13:30 UK in three passes - advance, second, third.
profile.why_gold: Matters for the growth half of the picture, but it is backward-looking by up to four months.
profile.watch: The advance reading is the only one that reliably moves anything. Later revisions rarely register.
profile.gotchas: Gold typically shrugs off GDP unless the miss is large or it confirms an existing recession narrative.

profile.name: Core PCE Price Index
profile.what: The Fed's preferred inflation gauge, stripped of food and energy. Released 13:30 UK.
profile.why_gold: It is the measure the Fed's 2% target is actually written against, so it carries more policy weight than CPI even though it moves markets less.
profile.watch: The m/m figure to two decimal places, and the three- and six-month annualised runs that commentators compute from it.
profile.gotchas: Largely predictable from the CPI and PPI released earlier in the month, so the surprise is usually small - which is exactly why a surprise here hits hard.

profile.name: Initial Jobless Claims
profile.what: New unemployment benefit filings in the prior week. Released every Thursday at 13:30 UK.
profile.why_gold: The highest-frequency labour signal available. Individually minor, but a trend of rising claims shifts the whole rate narrative.
profile.watch: The four-week moving average rather than the weekly print, and continuing claims for whether people are finding new work.
profile.gotchas: Distorted by holidays, weather and state-level administrative quirks. One bad week means nothing.
